research_conclusion: The cost-robustness question could not be answered as posed because the signal under test does not implement momentum. Evidence: (1) momentum_signals and mean_reversion_signals both compute ret = mean(log(closes[i-lookback+1:i+1])) and threshold its sign; for any series priced above 1 that quantity is positive at every bar, so momentum is a constant +1 (static long) and reversal a constant -1 (static short). (2) diag_momentum_signal.py: AAPL/AMZN/JPM at lookbacks 3/5/10 show ~4455-4462 active bars, positive=all, negative=0, exactly 1 sign change over ~17 years; sign agreement with the intended trailing-return direction is 0.536-0.604 (≈ base rate); mean-log-price quantity is positive 100% of the time. (3) The cost grid reproduces this: per-asset segment medians are identical across lookbacks 3/5/10 and essentially unchanged from 0.0x to 2.0x costs (AAPL +0.070, AMZN +0.076, JPM +0.083), because there is almost no turnover to charge; only NVDA flips negative at 5.0x. (4) The framework REGIME_STABLE count rises 6->7->8 as costs rise, which is a null-collapse artifact (the coin-flip null's ~112 changes/yr is devastated by costs), confirming that the framework verdict must not be read as edge evidence under costs. Independent verification: all five gates MATCH, including a fresh walk_forward + noise_benchmark path that reproduces every AMZN/JPM cand and null median, and a zero-cost cross-check that reproduces momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json exactly. Conclusion: the as-implemented candidate is COST_ROBUST but the classification is vacuous; the prior momentum evidence is confounded by a signal-construction defect and must not be treated as a momentum anomaly. This is durable, verified negative evidence with a precise, reproducible root cause.
